scope_notes: The initial raw-run harness did not yet fail closed on historical model/support-source/config identity. This audit independently verifies both reports against the old full config and source hashes; later harness versions add assertions. Initial report script hash is retained, not replaced by the current script hash.
The old record did not save raw gradient arrays or initial weight tensors. Auto reproduces all old retained numerical summaries; bitwise identity to unavailable old arrays is not claimed.
Power-of-two scaling produces exactly equal normalized gradients in every tensor of both backends, in both profiles. This demonstrates tested homogeneity, not every possible Jacobian property.

CE-norm scaling multiplies the old random direction until its norm matches a real MQAR mean-CE cotangent measured on separate valid examples at the same weights. It is not the actual CE gradient direction and is not substituted for the separate actual-loss investigation.

The FP64 reference is naive autograd with the identical FP32-representable weights/cotangent promoted to FP64; default LayerNorm and noRoPE avoid the model branches that explicitly force FP32. Tiled was never run or claimed as FP64.

Legacy failures remain at raw scale and after dividing the non-power-of-two CE-scale gradients back to raw scale. Both naive and tiled show this behavior; all independent normwise checks pass without changing thresholds.

Only about9–10percent of raw failing coordinates meet the predefined0.001RMS near-zero definition. Broader cancellation/rounding-sensitive coordinates also fail; no claim that every failure is near zero is made.

This classification is specific to the reproduced D32/T128/B2/V256 initialization fixture. Actual masked-CE, retained trained weights, optimizer deltas and intended StageB widths/batches are separate clearance evidence.
